newsitem.title: SPAIN: Asturiana waves goodbye to futures shackle.
newsitem.headline: Asturiana waves goodbye to futures shackle.

text.p: Spain's Asturiana de Zinc said on Friday it had put its problematic zinc futures position behind it but as a result had been forced to revise downward its forecasts for 1996.
The zinc producer said it had gradually liquidated its big loss-making zinc position on the London Metal Exchange (LME) through Glencore International from January until Thursday.
"We have finally disposed of this great risk caused by an enormous error. It was not without cost, but we managed it in an acceptable way," Asturiana Chairman Rafael Benjumea told journalists.
Asturiana has never disclosed the size of its position which it started to build in 1992, but analysts said that it grew to over one million tonnes during 1993.
The position had been blamed for zinc's poor two-year performance, but the company said by selling the position slowly through the year it had minimised the impact on prices.
"But the liquidation will increase financial costs for the year to around 2.71 billion pesetas," the company warned in a statment.
The main expense, however, would come from maintainance costs the position clocked up during the year, which the company has estimated at 5.20 billion pesetas.

"With a view to the evolution of zinc prices during the third quarter (which hit a year low) and the actions taken to liquidate the futures position, we have proceeded to revise downward the forecasted results for 1996," the company said in a statement.

Forecasts for attributable losses for the full year were consequently downgraded to a loss of 2.68 billion pesetas compared with a loss of 11.084 billion pesetas in 1995. The company did not give previous estimates for full year results.

Although the company downgraded full-year net operating result to a profit of 5.34 billion pesetas, it said it would still show an exceptional rebound from the previous year when it posted a loss of 8.54 billion pesetas.
In the first nine months of 1996, the company said net operating result was 3.15 billion pesetas compared with 849 million in the corresponding period of 1995.

"The average price of zinc in the third quarter was $1,002.76 per tonne, the lowest this year. But (despite) this, we have obtained a result in ordinary activities of 1.89 billion pesetas reflecting improvements in all commercial and industrial activities in the company," Asturiana said in a statement.

The company said the costs associated with the futures position would not be included until the annual results because the final liquidation had not been carried out until after the close of the third quarter.

Asturiana started taking long positions in zinc in 1992, when the annual price averaged $1,221 a tonne. It reported that the position reached its maximum volume during 1993 when zinc averaged $978.50.
In December, 1995 it passed the position to Swiss-based trader Glencore International to manage and by March, Asturiana said the position had been reduced by half, although it was still substantial.
Traders have said that the sale of the position would remove a significant cap from the zinc market.
